title: Week 5 Analysis
subtitle: Cadegn stood still and still leads by 13. Mike T jumped from 6th to 2nd.
intro_paragraphs: Four divisions reshuffled this week: the Ravens took the AFC North back from the Browns, the Packers climbed to second in the NFC North, the Broncos passed the Raiders for second in the AFC West, and the bottom of the AFC South and NFC South flipped. The middle of the pack moved a lot. The leader didn't move at all.
Note: these standings are through Week 5 only. Thursday's Week 6 game (Broncos 17, Seahawks 14 in OT) was taken out, so Denver is counted at 3-2 and Seattle at 3-2.

fun_facts.heading: Mike T Goes From 6th to 2nd
fun_facts.body: Mike T gained 15 points, the biggest jump of the week, going from 37 to 52. Points came in from four divisions. The biggest was the AFC West, where Denver moving into second matched Mike T's Chiefs-Broncos top two for +6. The Ravens retaking first in the AFC North, the Titans dropping to last in the AFC South, and the Packers moving into second in the NFC North each added 3 more. Mike T is now tied with Hume at 52, and the two are still tied after the first four tiebreakers: one perfect division, two top-2 bonuses, one bottom-2 bonus, and 12 exact hits each.

fun_facts.heading: Cadegn's Lead Holds at Zero Change
fun_facts.body: Cadegn finished the week at 65, exactly where they started. They lost 3 in the AFC North when Baltimore moved from second to first, and 3 in the NFC North when the Bears fell out of second. They got it back with Tennessee dropping to last in the AFC South and New Orleans dropping to last in the NFC South, both matching Cadegn's picks. The lead shrank from 20 to 13, but Cadegn is still the only bettor with two perfect divisions, and the AFC East and NFC East both held this week.

fun_facts.heading: Hume Edges Past Tom
fun_facts.body: Hume picked up 9 points, 6 of them in the AFC West with the same Chiefs-Broncos top two as Mike T. Tom gained 6 to reach 51 and is now 4th, one point behind the tie for 2nd. Dustin added 9 and sits at 49, so 2nd through 5th are covered by just 3 points. Houston passing Tennessee in the AFC South was worth 3 to six of the seven bettors, since almost everybody had the Titans last.

fun_facts.heading: Dilger and Farmer Slide
fun_facts.body: Dilger (-3) and Farmer (-6) were the only bettors whose totals went down. Both had Baltimore second in the AFC North and Chicago second in the NFC North, and both of those moved. Farmer was also the one bettor who had Tennessee third instead of last, so the Houston-Tennessee swap cost them 3 while it paid everyone else; a Saints-to-last move in the NFC South got 3 back. They're last at 30 and are still the only bettor without a perfect division. Dilger is 6th at 37, 12 points out of 5th.

fun_facts.heading: The Locks: Same Four Holding
fun_facts.body:
4 of the 8 preseason unanimous picks are holding, the same four as last week: the Bills first and the Patriots second in the AFC East, the Steelers third in the AFC North, and the Cardinals last in the NFC West. Buffalo is now 5 for 5.

The Rams are 0 for 5 as the unanimous NFC West winner pick while the 49ers are 5-0, and the Lions are still chasing a 5-0 Minnesota. The Raiders, picked unanimously to finish last in the AFC West, are 3-2 while the Chargers are 0-5.

fun_facts.heading: One Fewer Surprise Division Leader
fun_facts.body: The Ravens taking back the AFC North means three divisions are now led by teams nobody in the pool picked to win: the Vikings, Panthers, and 49ers. That helped Mike T, Dustin, and Tom, who all had Baltimore. Mike T and Cadegn now lead with 3 of 8 division-winner picks currently correct. Dilger is at 1 of 8.

closing_paragraph: Cadegn is still 13 points clear, but 2nd through 5th are separated by 3 points, and Mike T showed this week that one good Sunday can move someone four spots. Same time next Tuesday.
